objective: Assess the feasibility of animal-to-human PMB exposure prediction and efficacious-dose estimation using preclinical PK/PD (SC001).

study.regimen: Partial, separate regimen information: mouse dose-fractionation schedules, rat IV administration, and horse single- and repeated-dose summaries (SC007, SC008, SC012).
study.population: Mouse, rat, rabbit, held-out healthy and hospitalized horses, K. pneumoniae, and a human validation cohort (SC007, SC008, SC010, SC012, SC014, SC016).
study.system: Animal-to-human systemic and pulmonary PK with preclinical antibacterial PK/PD (SC019, SC024, SC027, SC028).
study.measurements: Concentration-time, binding, susceptibility and antibacterial-response evidence (SC007, SC008, SC010, SC012, SC014, SC016).
study.methods: Data preparation, animal PK modeling, interspecies prediction, PK/PD regression, independent human validation and PTA (SC018, SC019, SC024, SC027, SC028, SC029).

items.statement: Test whether animal PK and preclinical PK/PD can predict human PMB exposure and support efficacious-dose estimation. The primary outcome is model feasibility, not a clinical dosing recommendation or proof of generalizability.
PMB is a known-drug test case with existing human PK intended for independent validation.
PMB is the sole test drug; colistin and other antibiotics cannot substitute for it.

The planned translational approach follows the objective of Sou et al. (2021), Model-Informed Drug Development for Antimicrobials: Translational PK and PK/PD Modeling to Predict an Efficacious Human Dose for Apramycin, Clinical Pharmacology & Therapeutics 109:1063-1073, doi:10.1002/cpt.2104.
Do not import the apramycin model or its parameters into this project.
The proposal identifies PMB_source_tables_by_species.xlsx as the single animal and in-vitro workbook; its sheets retain source-shaped tables and notes rather than a ready-made modeling dataset.

The mouse workbook resources comprise plasma and ELF PK, serum-binding inputs (SC020), strain MICs, dose-fractionation schedules, bacterial-burden endpoints and digitized index-response panels. Panel matching is addressed in MI001.
The rat workbook resources comprise individual IV plasma profiles, serum and seven-tissue biodistribution means, and serum binding measured by dialysis and ultrafiltration.
The proposal cautions that the limited rat observations do not establish predictive validity.

The rabbit workbook resources comprise mean plasma, ELF and whole-lung profiles, exposure summaries, pulmonary infection outcomes and study metadata. Related unresolved issues are MI002, MI003 and MI004.

Assess whether rabbit evidence identifies a model component or supports only exploratory constraints. Use it only to the extent it identifies a component, document exclusion or exploratory use, and preserve source discrepancies.

The held-out horse resources comprise digitized serum concentrations from two veterinary studies—healthy-horse peaks and troughs and hospitalized-horse daily samples—and printed single- and repeated-dose summaries from a third study. Dose-basis and binding limitations are MI005 and MI006.
Horse data cannot be used for fitting, model selection or scaling. Their permitted translation-check procedure is SC025.

The In_vitro_MIC resources comprise K. pneumoniae time-kill data for BAA1705, KP619 and three KPC-2 isolates at two static concentrations; genotype and MIC data for six carbapenem-resistant isolates; and a surveillance MIC distribution.
Use eligible time-kill data for PD and the surveillance MIC distribution for population-weighted attainment; that distribution cannot replace matched strain MICs.

The described human validation resources are a 40-patient dataset containing 230 concentration records and 268 dose events, together with human reference tables. Availability and release conditions are recorded in MI007.

The proposal assigns these resource roles: PMB_project_proposal.docx defines the task; AGENT_README.md explains package use and known gaps; benchmark_reference.json contains final-stage reference material, including published model-derived parameters and targets. Scientific-result access restrictions are in SC034.

Planned preparation splits mixed source blocks into PK, PD, MIC, validation and benchmark inputs; checks provenance, units, dose histories, experimental units and missing fields; and identifies usable records and unresolved gaps before fitting.

Planned animal PK work selects eligible systemic and, where supported, pulmonary models for mouse, rat and rabbit, evaluating fit, parameter identifiability and held-out prediction where the design permits. Rabbit use is governed by SC011.
Two mouse serum-binding sources conflict: about 91% versus 97–99% bound. Resolution is tracked in MI008.
Rat serum-binding sources conflict: 80% versus 92–99% bound. Resolution is tracked in MI009.

Separate routes, formulations, analytes, total versus unbound drug, and plasma, serum, whole-lung tissue, BAL and ELF. Record a justification for every conversion or physiological bridge, and do not force unsupported pulmonary or multi-species models.
Never average the conflicting binding sources in SC020 and SC021; carry fu as a sensitivity parameter.

Planned translation uses supported animal models, body size, protein binding and justified physiological relationships; rat evidence is intended for pulmonary translation only where supported. Compare scaling with and without each species rather than assuming more species is better.

After mouse, rat and rabbit scaling is frozen, predict horse profiles under the reported horse doses and compare them with the held-out horse figures as an intermediate test of prediction in a large-body-weight species. Record the result without retuning.

Planned human prediction produces concentration-time profiles, AUC and Cmax with uncertainty under specified doses and routes, then freezes these predictions before opening human outcomes. Prediction scenarios are addressed in MI010.

For eligible K. pneumoniae data, including eligible mouse PD evidence, compare fAUC/MIC, fCmax/MIC and fT>MIC using ordinary Emax and sigmoid Emax/Hill regression. Estimate supported exposure targets, or report that the available data cannot determine a best index or target. Pending determinations are MI012 and MI013.

Under the freezing prerequisite in SC036, planned human validation applies the model to actual human dose histories and compares predicted and observed plasma PK, assessing ELF separately when compatible data exist. Report bias, precision, exposure agreement and predictive uncertainty against the prespecified criteria. Related unresolved items are MI007, MI014 and MI015.

After PK validation and PD qualification, simulate a prespecified human population and dosing scenarios to estimate PTA at each MIC, and include an exploratory efficacious-dose estimate where supported. Scenario choices are MI016 and MI017; uncertainty handling is SC038.
Deliver PTA tables and curves, the feasibility conclusion, uncertainty, the final published-result benchmark and reproducible code. If required inputs are missing, report why PTA is not estimable.

Keep source identifiers, units, missing values and BLQ limits. Do not treat group means or digitized observations as individual animals, or invent IDs, variability, exposure-response links or missing measurements; specifically, group summaries cannot supply invented interindividual variability.

Give all three indices in SC027 equal eligibility. Compare the indices and both regression families on the same matched response records, strain MICs, free-exposure basis, dosing histories, time windows and likelihood. Register the selection rule before regression fitting; report R², AIC/BIC, stability and identifiability, counting the extra Hill parameter. Do not select by R² alone or force a winner. The selection rule is tracked in MI011.
Keep stasis, 1-log kill and 2-log kill targets separate; other pathogens cannot set K. pneumoniae targets.

Keep scientific results in benchmark_reference.json hidden during selection. Published fitted parameters and model-derived results cannot set primary-analysis starting values, bounds, priors or rankings; reserve them for the final benchmark.
Human outcomes cannot tune the animal model or scaling.
Freeze the model and validation criteria before their validation step, and freeze PD targets before dose simulation. MIC-input freezing is specified in SC037.

For MIC/PTA processing, preserve MIC bins, units, counts/proportions, denominators and censored categories; derive probabilities transparently and freeze the MIC distribution/input before dose simulation. Never silently renormalize incomplete coverage. Report per-MIC PTA separately from MIC-weighted attainment. Coverage assessment is MI018.
Include supported PK variability in PTA and propagate parameter, binding, PD-target and MIC uncertainty, subject to SC031. Variability support is addressed in MI019.
Do not interpret a successful fit as predictive validation, or human PK agreement as validation of antibacterial efficacy or safety.
Save transformations, assumptions, code, seeds and results.
Obtain human review before fitting.
The selected proposal is Animal to Human Translation of Polymyxin B, feasibility study Version 3.0 (draft), dated 8 October 2026; it states that it supersedes earlier versions.
Prior approvals do not automatically carry forward to this proposal.
Preserve the original validation result if a later model is revised.
Preserve failures and data gaps in the documented conclusions.

items.impact: Mouse panels cannot be treated as matched regimen-level exposure-response records without verification.
items.why_it_matters: The proposal explicitly states that separate mouse panels are not verified matched regimen records; attachment bodies have not been searched.
items.clarification: Verify the panel, regimen, strain-MIC and response associations required by SC032, documenting supported matches and unresolved links.

items.field: Additional public rabbit PMB concentration evidence
items.impact: The reported availability limit must inform the eligibility assessment of rabbit evidence.
items.why_it_matters: The proposal reports that no further public rabbit PMB concentration data were found. This does not establish absence from all sources or unread attachment contents.
items.clarification: Record the scope and consequences of this source-reported availability limit during adequacy assessment.

items.impact: The decision to include a rabbit model component or retain exploratory constraints remains pending.
items.why_it_matters: The assessment required by SC011 has not been supplied; workbook contents have not been inspected.
items.clarification: Assess component identifiability and record the inclusion, exclusion or exploratory-use decision under SC011.

items.impact: Rabbit source values cannot be reconciled or selected without identifying the discrepancies.
items.why_it_matters: The proposal flags rabbit source discrepancies but does not specify their affected values or contexts; attachment bodies remain unsearched.
items.clarification: Identify and preserve the rabbit discrepancies with their source, study, matrix and measurement context, without silently resolving them.

items.impact: The dose basis limits interpretation of held-out horse predictions and any mass-dose comparison.
items.why_it_matters: Horse doses are mostly reported in IU without salt or base correction; a supported mass-equivalent basis is unresolved.
items.clarification: Clarify each horse study's reported dose basis and any supported salt/base correction, retaining reported units and documenting unresolved limitations for SC025.

items.impact: Binding-dependent interpretation of the held-out horse translation requires an explicit limitation or justified handling.
items.why_it_matters: The proposal explicitly states that no horse binding is available.
items.clarification: Document how SC025 will be interpreted without horse-binding evidence; do not invent a binding value.

items.impact: Human validation cannot use the protected resources before their authorized release.
items.why_it_matters: Human validation data are not in the supplied package. The dataset and reference tables described in SC016 are held in a separate file and released only at task 5, after the animal model, scaling and predictions are frozen.
items.clarification: Release the separate human validation file only at the stated task and after all stated freezing conditions are met.

items.impact: Mouse free-exposure calculations and binding-dependent translation require sensitivity handling of the conflicting sources.
items.why_it_matters: The conflicting mouse binding values are preserved in SC020; their contextual reconciliation and sensitivity treatment remain unresolved.
items.clarification: Identify the source definitions and experimental contexts and define justified mouse fu sensitivity handling under SC023.

items.impact: Rat free-exposure calculations and binding-dependent translation require sensitivity handling of the conflicting sources.
items.why_it_matters: The conflicting rat binding values are preserved in SC021; their contextual reconciliation and sensitivity treatment remain unresolved.
items.clarification: Identify the source definitions and experimental contexts and define justified rat fu sensitivity handling under SC023.

items.field: Human PK prediction doses and routes
items.impact: The human concentration-time, AUC and Cmax prediction scenarios cannot be fully defined.
items.why_it_matters: The supplied proposal requires specified human prediction doses and routes in SC026 but does not supply those choices; this is not a finding about unread files.
items.clarification: Specify the human PK prediction dosing scenarios, including their doses and routes, before generating and freezing predictions.

items.impact: Index ranking cannot proceed without the preregistered comparison rule.
items.why_it_matters: SC032 requires registration before regression fitting, but the proposal does not supply the rule.
items.clarification: Register the selection rule before fitting, retaining SC032's comparison conditions and prohibition on forcing a winner.

items.why_it_matters: SC027 explicitly allows the outcome that available eligible data cannot determine a best index; no completed comparison is supplied.
items.clarification: Assess index discrimination using eligible matched data and report indeterminacy if the evidence does not support selection.

items.impact: PD qualification and subsequent target-attainment simulation depend on whether supported targets can be estimated.
items.why_it_matters: Target estimation in SC027 is conditional on support and has not been performed in the supplied proposal.
items.clarification: Assess which exposure targets are estimable under SC033 and report when no supported target can be determined.

items.impact: Human predictive performance cannot receive a prespecified acceptance judgment.
items.why_it_matters: The criteria required by SC028 and SC036 are not specified in the proposal.
items.clarification: Fix the criteria for bias, precision, exposure agreement and predictive uncertainty before validation.

items.impact: The conditional ELF branch of human validation cannot yet be determined.
items.why_it_matters: SC028 requires separate ELF assessment when compatible data exist; compatibility and availability have not been assessed in the supplied proposal.
items.clarification: At authorized validation access, determine whether compatible human ELF evidence exists and document the separate assessment or its limitation.

items.impact: PTA population simulation cannot be defined.
items.why_it_matters: SC029 requires a prespecified human population, but the proposal supplies no population specification for PTA.
items.clarification: Prespecify the human PTA population before simulation.

items.impact: PTA regimen comparisons and exploratory efficacious-dose estimation cannot be defined.
items.why_it_matters: SC029 requires prespecified dosing scenarios for the later PTA phase, distinct from the human PK prediction inputs in MI010.
items.clarification: Prespecify the PTA dosing scenarios before simulation, after the stated PK-validation and PD-qualification prerequisites.

items.impact: The distribution's suitability for population-weighted attainment remains unassessed.
items.why_it_matters: SC037 requires explicit treatment of coverage; the proposal supplies no completed coverage assessment, and the workbook has not been searched.
items.clarification: Assess and document surveillance MIC coverage before accepting the distribution for weighted attainment, retaining any incomplete coverage explicitly.

items.impact: The variability basis for PTA simulation remains unqualified.
items.why_it_matters: The proposal requires supported PK variability but supplies no completed assessment of whether defensible individual variability can be supported.
items.clarification: Assess which PK variability is defensible for PTA and specify its use under SC031 and SC038 before simulation.
